Operations: head, options and trace were dropped, and so were OpenAPI 3.2's
query and additionalOperations. Every Path Item operation is now generated.
Servers map the methods Spring's RequestMethod has no constant for (QUERY,
PURGE...) with a generated @HttpMethodMapping, which a generated

Spring still answers the others, 405 included, and it answers 406/415 for a
request of its method it cannot serve. Such operations declare what they
consume, since Spring reads a @RequestBody's content type only for
POST/PUT/PATCH. Clients send them with HttpMethod.valueOf; Spring Boot 2
clients, whose HttpMethod is an enum, fail the generation instead.

  string, is read as that object sent form-exploded (any other media type
  fails); clients used to take it and never send it;
- a $ref to components/mediaTypes is resolved (it crashed the generator);
- a response without description is documented with its summary;

(or application/stream+json) is detected from the contract; its schema, the items

  not overridden, and a plain method to implement returning
  ResponseEntity<Stream<T>> (or taking a Stream<T> body). The generated

  the items, gets its own endpoint picked by the Accept header.

  and return Flux<T>; ApiWebClient reads and writes NDJSON and sends Publisher
  bodies.

  operation and asks for reactive=true.

several media types renders a valid @ApiResponse content array.

8.2.1: honour requestBody.required, clean re-extracted contract jars, drop @Size(max = 0) (#471)

* Honour requestBody.required, empty re-extracted contract jars, and drop @Size(max = 0)

requestBody.required: the model read whether the `required` key existed,
not its value, so an explicit `required: false` came out required; for a
$ref'd body (components/requestBodies) it read the $ref node instead of
the resolved body, so `required: true` came out optional. Server
templates (imperative and reactive) then emitted a bare @RequestBody,
always required. Now the value is read from the resolved body, servers
emit @RequestBody(required = false) for optional bodies, and the
RestClient/WebClient client classes only reject a null body the contract
requires. @HttpExchange already used the value. OpenAPI's default for a
missing `required` is false, which these now follow.

Contract jars: when a SNAPSHOT changed, its jar was unzipped on top of
the previous extraction, so files the new build no longer carries (a
conventional contract/openapi.yaml) were still found and generated from.
The folder is now emptied before re-extracting. The log names the
extracted file actually read, and the errors list every conventional
path (.yml and .yaml).

@Size: a field with only minLength got @Size(max = 0, min = N), and the
validator read 0 as "no limit", so a contract maxLength: 0 was not
enforced. It now gets max = Integer.MAX_VALUE and the validator compares
plainly. Models keep both attributes, so a Size annotation left from an
earlier generation still compiles.

the imperative and reactive servers and the HttpExchange, RestClient and
WebClient clients, plus a re-extraction test.

  URI template variables, so each value is encoded exactly once and an

Everything is opt-in; with no new configuration callMode generates what it
did before.

For every Spring Boot version (2, 3, 4), using only RestTemplate/WebClient:
- ApiRestClient(RestTemplate[, authentications]) and
  ApiWebClient(WebClient[, authentications]) use a configured client
  instead of building one.
- Each *Api has a basePath (the first `servers` URL by default) settable by
  constructor or setter, and constructors taking its ApiRestClient or
  ApiWebClient. An empty base path resolves requests against the client's

For Spring Boot 3+ (typically 4), `useHttpExchange=true` generates each

relative paths, contract parameter bindings, @RequestPart per multipart
part), to be backed by the service's RestClient/WebClient through

ApiRestClient/ApiWebClient, auth classes or server URL are generated then.

The reactive client class also stops failing generation on a parameter
without a description, on responses without a body, and no longer declares

* Fix #451: Type arrays of refs to a named primitive schema as lists of that primitive

`states: {type: array, items: {$ref: State}}` with `State: {type: string}`
generated `List<StateDTO>`, where StateDTO wraps the value in an object. On
the wire each element is the bare value (`{"states": ["ACTIVE"]}`), so the
list could not be read or written as the contract describes (400s against
existing consumers). A non-array property with the same $ref was already

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix #452: Name clashing inline schemas after their parent instead of merging them

An inline schema's class is named after the property that declares it, so
inline schemas of different shapes under the same property name in
different schemas (three `services` arrays, say) were all written to one
ServicesDTO: the last one processed won, and every other property was typed
with its shape, silently dropping fields such as `service_id`.

Before building models, the contract is scanned for property names that
declare more than one inline shape (or clash with a named schema); only
those classes are named after their parent too (NewSalesPointServicesDTO).
Names without a clash keep their class names, and the result does not
depend on processing order. An Inline* wrapper lends its bare name
(Response200GetItems) so its class keeps the model prefix and suffix.

Also takes an inline object property's JSON name from the property, not
the referenced schema: `config: {$ref: .../configuration}` was serialised

* Fix #447: Type properties that $ref an allOf schema without 'type'

ApiTool.getType reports a schema with no `type` as "" rather than null, so

A property that $refs a composition declaring only allOf/anyOf/oneOf thus got

* Fix #448: Mark allOf properties required only when a 'required' list names them

processAllOf forced required on every member's fields, and passed the $ref
node rather than the schema it resolves to, so no `required` list was ever
consulted. Every property of an allOf model became @NonNull / validated /

A property is now required when a `required` list on any member, or on the
composing schema, names it (a value must satisfy every member), and it is
not nullable, matching how plain objects are handled.

testRefToAllOfProperty assets change accordingly: none of their allOf

solvePathRefs loads each external path item file and inlines every file

Fix: Make the generated REST and web clients compile against Spring Boot 4 (#446)

* Fix: Make the generated clients compile against Spring Boot 4

The Jackson 3 branch of the REST client template imported
AbstractJacksonHttpMessageConverter from org.springframework.http.converter.json,
but Spring Framework 7 puts it in the parent package, so every generated
ApiRestClient failed to compile under Spring Boot 4.

Compiling the generated clients against spring-web 7.0.9 surfaced four more
APIs that Spring Framework 7 dropped:

- HttpHeaders no longer implements MultiValueMap, so containsKey and
  entrySet are gone. The containsKey guard around remove was redundant, and
  forEach iterates headers on both Spring 6 and 7.
- UriComponentsBuilder.fromHttpUrl gave way to fromUriString.
- ClientHttpResponse.getRawStatusCode gave way to getStatusCode().value().
- org.springframework.util.Base64Utils gave way to java.util.Base64.
  HttpBearerAuth imported it without ever using it.

Every replacement already exists in Spring Framework 6.1, so the templates
stay free of Spring Boot version branching: only the converter import, which
is Jackson 3 specific, sits inside the existing isJackson3 block.

Verified by compiling the expected assets with javac against real jars:
Spring 7.0.9 with Jackson 3.1.6 and Spring 6.2.17 with Jackson 2.19, for both
the REST client and the web client.

`client-ref`, `delivery.status` - was emitted verbatim, and the generated code
did not compile:

    public ShipmentV3Dto createShipmentV3(String Idempotency-Key, ...)
    private String client-ref;

Reserved words were already handled; the character set was not.

`StringCaseUtils.toJavaIdentifier` now rebuilds such a name in lower camel case
out of its alphanumeric runs, prefixing `_` when the result would start with a
digit (`2fa-token` -> `_2faToken`). A name that already is a legal identifier is
returned untouched, so nothing that compiles today is renamed.
`toJavaVariableName` adds the reserved-word prefix on top, for the positions
that declare a variable on their own.

The contract name is not replaced anywhere it travels over the wire. It stays
in `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@JsonProperty`, `@Schema`, in the URI
variables and in the header, query and cookie maps the clients fill; only the
Java identifier is adapted. `ParameterObject.getVariableName` and
`SchemaFieldObject.getFieldName` expose the identifier to the templates, which
keep reading `name`/`baseName` for the wire.

Header and cookie parameters also gain the binding they never had: the API
interface declared them with no annotation at all, so Spring resolved them as
request parameters. They are now bound with `@RequestHeader(name = ...)` and
`@CookieValue(name = ...)`, and `@RequestParam` carries an explicit `name` when
the identifier no longer matches the contract name.

Verified end to end: the generated interface, rest client and web client
compile, and the model round-trips `{"client-ref":"abc"}` through Jackson under
that name.

Fix #443: Model propertyless compositions and drop nameless fields (#444)

* Fix #443: Model propertyless compositions and drop nameless fields

Four defects around schemas that declare nothing modellable, and around
how allOf members are combined.

**Nameless fields.** Every template interpolates the field name, so a field
without one cannot be rendered. `ApiTool.getName` returns null for any node
that is not parameter-like, so a schema modelled as a single field could
produce a field with a blank name. `resolveFieldName` now falls back to the
name of the schema being built, and a field still left unnamed is dropped
rather than carried into a template that cannot render it.

**Propertyless compositions.** `anyOf: [{type: object}]` produced a class
with no fields, which parses and compiles but silently drops every value it
receives. Such a composition now falls back to the free-form `Object`
(`List<Object>` inside an array), and logs a warning naming the property and
the combinator, so the fallback is never a silent surprise. The composed
schema is also no longer registered in `compositedSchemas` when it turns out
to describe no property, so no empty class is emitted for it.

**allOf required flags.** Every member re-marked the whole accumulated set as
required, so a property contributed by an earlier member became required
because a later member existed. Members are now collected separately and only
their own fields are marked.

**allOf narrowing.** A value has to satisfy every member, so when two members
declare the same property the most specific declaration is the accurate one.
A member that types a property another member left free-form now replaces it,
instead of the result depending on set iteration order.

Fix #440, #441: Reserved words in generated identifiers and JSON names (#442)

* Sanitize every generated identifier derived from a Java reserved word

Reserved-word handling was applied to field names only, so any other
identifier the model templates derive from a schema or property name could
come out as a Java keyword and fail to compile.

Three such identifiers:

- The singular adder of a collection was singularized *after* being
  sanitized, so the singular form never reached the reserved-word check:
  `packages` produced `package(Package package)` and `interfaces` produced
  `interface(String interface)`. Sanitizing now happens last, through
  `calculateSingularSafeName`, which also keeps the adder distinct from the
  plural setter when the two collapse onto the same name (`new` keeps
  yielding `__new`).
- `build()` and `equals()` declared a local variable named after the class
  in lower camel case, so a schema named `Package` produced
  `Package package = new Package(this);`.
- The builder setter of an enum property sanitized the method name but not
  its parameter, producing `_package(Package package)` with an undefined
  right-hand side. The committed asyncapi rare-chars assets had this
  captured as `_new(New new)`, which does not compile; they are corrected
  here.

Adds testReservedWordsGeneration for OpenAPI, which had no reserved-word
coverage at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix #440: Serialize reserved-word properties under their contract name

The `@JsonProperty` value was generated from the sanitized Java identifier
rather than from the property name the contract declares, so a property
named `new` was written to and read from the wire as `_new`. The Java field
still has to be renamed; the JSON name must not be.

The field annotation alone is not enough. Models are deserialized through
`@JsonDeserialize(builder = ...)`, and Jackson introspects the builder, not
the value class, so the builder setter needs the annotation as well -
without it `{"new": [...]}` fails with UnrecognizedPropertyException. The
singular adder and the map `...Value` helper are convenience methods rather
than properties and stay unannotated.

The name is taken with `?uncap_first`, matching what `@Schema(name = ...)`
already does: for a property resolved through a `$ref` the engine reports
the referenced schema name (`Schema`) rather than the property name
(`schema`), and the two annotations have to agree.

Verified with a Jackson round trip: `{"new":["n1"],"tags":["t1"]}` now
binds, and serialization emits `new`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix #441: Avoid the getClass() collision for a property named class

Accessors were built as `get`/`set` + the capitalized property name, with no
reserved-word check. For most keywords that is harmless (`package` yields a
perfectly legal `getPackage()`), but a property named `class` yields
`getClass()`, which cannot override the final `Object.getClass()`, so the
model never compiles.

`calculateAccessorSuffix` now falls back to the sanitized field name for
exactly that case, giving `get_class()` / `set_class()`. Both accessors are
renamed together so that they keep agreeing with the field on the implicit
Jackson property name (`_class`), which `@JsonProperty("class")` then maps
back to the contract name. No other accessor changes.

The OpenAPI reserved-words fixture now carries a `class` property; its model
compiles and round-trips `{"class":"express"}` through Jackson.

Covers what the contract keeps (the JSON names) and what the Java side
adapts (fields, builder methods, collection adders, the class accessors),
plus the Lombok caveat.

Fix #438: Resolve specs declared with fromGroupId from the configured repositories (#439)

* Fix #438: Resolve specs declared with fromGroupId from the configured repositories

The v7.1 fields fromGroupId/fromArtifactId/fromVersion were accepted by the
configuration model but never used when the contract was read: OpenApiGenerator
always loaded filePath from the module's filesystem, so a spec published as an
artifact failed with "Error reading api file: <module>/<filePath>". They were
only consulted in OpenApiUtil.processPaths, after the document had already been
parsed, and that path could not work either -- resolveMavenArtifact built its
path with a format string holding eight placeholders for ten arguments, so it
looked for <artifact>/<version>-/.jar in ~/.m2, and nothing ever downloaded the
artifact from a repository. AsyncAPI never had the fields at all: the Gradle
task set them dynamically on a builder that has no such methods.

The contract is now resolved before anything reads it. The artifact is fetched
through a SpecArtifactResolver -- Maven Resolver in the Maven plugin, a detached
configuration in the Gradle one, so settings.xml repositories, mirrors and
credentials apply and private repositories work -- and unpacked once per build
under target/generated-resources/multiapi-specs. filePath is then rewritten to
the extracted copy, which is what makes a multi-file contract resolve its
relative $refs: they are ordinary files by the time the pipeline sees them,
instead of classpath lookups of the raw $ref value that only ever matched a
root-relative path.

- Engine: SpecArtifactResolver SPI, DependencySpecMaterializer (extract, cache
  per artifact, zip-slip guarded, error lists the specs the artifact carries),
  LocalRepositorySpecArtifactResolver as the no-build-tool fallback.
- ExternalSpecSource carries the coordinates for both OpenAPI and AsyncAPI specs
  and rejects half-declared ones instead of silently reading the filesystem.
- Gradle: the coordinates move from the task to each specFile, matching the
  Maven configuration and the documentation.
- Remove the URLClassLoader plumbing threaded through MapperPathUtil and
  SchemaUtil: it was only ever null, and solveRefFromJar matched $ref values
  verbatim as JAR resources, so it could not resolve a relative reference.
- Replace the placeholder tests, which asserted that string literals were
  non-empty, with tests that package a contract, resolve it and generate from
  it, plus a Gradle integration test that publishes the contract to a repository
  and deletes it from the project.
